subject: MSA redlines: liability cap mechanics and carve-outs
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procure@acme.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines & liability cap proposal

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our GC attached markups to your standard MSA (see Acme_MSA_redlines.pdf). Two points where we need clarity before we can route to procurement:

1) Liability cap — we want to cap Redwood's liability at the greater of (i) fees paid in the prior 12 months or (ii) $2M. We'd also like to propose that the cap is an aggregate cap for the contract term rather than an annualized cap.

2) Consequential damages carve-outs — we will accept the standard commercial carve-outs but request explicit carve-outs for (a) claims related to regulatory fines, and (b) losses stemming from data loss due to misconduct.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept an aggregate cap or whether you need to keep it annualized? Also, there are a few SLO-related carve-outs in our redlines that touch on uptime credits — we flagged those.

Sophie
Acme Corporation — Contracts

Attachment: Acme_MSA_redlines.pdf (PDF, 42 pages)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines & liability cap proposal

Sophie — thanks for the redlines and for flagging the two liability points. Quick answers up front:

- Aggregate vs. annualized: our standard approach is to tie the cap to an annualized basis (trailing 12 months fees) for predictable economics across renewals, but we can consider an aggregate cap for multi-year deals if there is a firm commitment / minimum spend.
- Consequential carve-outs: we do not take responsibility for regulatory fines; however, we treat breaches that result from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct differently and carve those into indemnity.

I'll loop in Laura (legal) and Karthik (solutions) to propose concrete language. If you have internal guidance on whether Acme will accept a floor (e.g., $1M) or a multiple of fees (e.g., 2x) that would help speed the review.

Proposed next step: I'll prepare a short counterproposal that shows (A) Redwood's preferred annualized cap: 2x trailing 12-month fees with a $1M floor; and (B) an alternate aggregate cap option (3x total contract fees) if you can commit to a minimum annual spend. Would that frame help?

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline-summary-20280719.xlsx (spreadsheet, 2 tabs)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA redlines & liability cap proposal (internal)

Marissa / Karthik — quick legal POV so we have language to send:

- We prefer annualized caps tied to revenue (trailing 12 months invoiced fees) because it aligns loss exposure with current consumption. It also avoids front-loading liability on the vendor for early-year problems in long-duration deals.
- If Acme insists on an aggregate cap, we should ask for a higher multiple (3x of fees paid) and a minimum spend commitment.
- Consequential damages: we should keep the standard limitation but accept carve-outs for death/bodily injury and willful misconduct. Do NOT accept carve-outs that broadly permit consequential recovery for regulatory fines — instead offer to include a limited carve-out for regulatory fines caused by Redwood's gross negligence, subject to cap and notice requirements.

Draft language I recommend (short):
"Redwood's aggregate liability for direct damages arising out of this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) fees paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim or (b) USD 1,000,000; provided, that in the event of any materially higher committed annual spend explicitly set forth in an Order Form, the parties shall negotiate an aggregate cap equal to three (3) times the total fees paid through the term. Notwithstanding the foregoing, liability for death, bodily injury and liability arising from Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence shall not be limited."

I'll tidy and send with redline markup after Marissa confirms approach.

—Laura
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines & liability cap proposal

Sophie — thanks for the patience. Attached is Redwood's counterproposal (RI_MSA_counter_redlines.pdf) and a short memo explaining the rationale. High level:

1) Primary position: annualized cap equal to the greater of (i) fees paid in the prior 12 months or (ii) USD 1,000,000. This keeps unit economics predictable and matches our standard practice.
2) Alternate (if Acme needs an aggregate cap): we can accept an aggregate cap equal to three (3) times the total contract fees, but only where Acme commits to a minimum annual spend (we proposed a minimum of USD 500k/year).
3) Consequential damages carve-outs: we will not accept unconstrained carve-outs for regulatory fines. We can offer a limited exception for regulatory fines caused by Redwood's gross negligence, subject to the same monetary cap and prompt notice/mitigation obligations.

Please review the attached and let us know which option you prefer. If you want to take the aggregate-cap route, confirm the expected annual spend so we can populate the Order Form.

Thanks — next step from our side after you pick a path: Laura will send the finalized MSA redline and we'll produce a DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Marissa

Attachment: RI_MSA_counter_redlines.pdf (PDF, 15 pages)
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procure@acme.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2028 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines & liability cap proposal

Marissa — appreciate the clear options and the rationale. Acme will accept Redwood's primary position (annualized cap: greater of prior 12 months fees or $1M) provided we get a limited carve-out for regulatory fines where the fines are directly caused by Redwood's willful misconduct; that carve-out should be subject to the same dollar cap. We also accept the limitation language for consequential damages otherwise.

Procurement asks that Laura's final redline include (i) a 30-day cure/notice requirement before indemnity triggers for regulatory claims, and (ii) insertion of the minimum-annual-spend clause as an optional seat (we will not accept a mandatory minimum at this time).

If that's acceptable, please send the final redline and DocuSign. We aim to get signatures in the week of Jul 23.

Thanks,
Sophie
